notes: Delete mirror of biology-replace-0019: the rule is removed. New members become not known (the rule was the only route); well-known members keep their value where it was stored by name and become not known where it was reached through the rule. Membership no longer needs to give way, since nothing clashes. R1: no snake eats plants; egg-, snail-, insect- and worm-eaters all count as carnivorous ('strictly carnivorous', Wikipedia). 'Carnivorous' is used, not 'carnivore', to avoid the order Carnivora. Well-known members: the boa constrictor and pythons, chosen because their names do not contain 'snake' and their diet is stated by name ('pythons are carnivores' 280; 'boa constrictor AND carnivorous' 132; boa diet of rodents 626). Avoided king cobra, anaconda and black mamba, whose superlatives ('longest venomous snake', 'heaviest snake') entail their snake membership. Pythons leaving the snake class has one side fact (the reticulated python stops being the longest snake), which is about the member itself, not a firm fact outside the chain; kept, as the ostrich in 0006. New members are named in the prompt with membership stated; the prompts give no habitat or prey hint. Near query asks a different relation of the same class (reptile), whose answer differs from 'herbivorous'. Verifier: snake frugivory is anecdotal only; no real exception to the rule. Genus route: Tantilla (centipede snakes) and Lycodon (wolf snakes) have some genus-level diet text ('Tantilla AND centipedes' 101, 'Lycodon AND lizards' 51), so a model that knows the genus could keep 'carnivorous' after the delete; accepted as small, as with the jumping spider in 0005.
